Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like August 2011, during the US debt-ceiling and downgrade turmoil.

- Unemployment at 9.1%, fed funds near 0.08%, and a 10-year yield of 2.19% (it fell sharply in August 2011).
- VIX at 32.89 is consistent with the August 2011 spike.
- Headline CPI at 3.59% year over year fits mid-2011, and so does core CPI at 1.76%.
- Gold is up 46% over 12 months, which fits a peak near $1,800 in August 2011.
- Payrolls averaging +72k over 3 months matches the weak summer 2011 numbers (June and July were weak, and August showed 0).
- Equities are down 2.6% over the month, with a 10% drawdown. The S&P fell about 5.7% in August 2011, so the month return does not fit perfectly. September 2011 saw a further decline of about 7%. The 2-year yield of 0.20% fits both months.
- Industrial production growth of 3.7% year over year also fits 2011.

The 3-month and 6-month equity returns of -6.8% and -7.6% could be August or September. In September 2011 the 10-year yield was about 1.92%, so 2.19% points to August. The VIX at the end of August 2011 was about 29.9 and at the end of September about 42.6, so 32.89 is not an exact match to either. The equity 1-month return of -2.6% is also off from August's -5.5%, though an end-of-month data timing difference might explain it. Overall, August remains the best fit.
